answer: A stake-weighted lottery allocates a stall at the jetty market, where vendors sell prism lamps and velvet fabric. Before the draw, each entrant locks funds, and the contract assigns one ticket per indivisible unit locked. Splitting a balance among N accounts yields the same total tickets and the same chance of winning. An attacker must lock more funds to improve those odds, assuming there are no free tickets per account and the draw is unbiased.
